brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit (storage shelving built from hex bases)
requirements.evidence: Five full hex bases plus two north-half bases on level 0 form a compact cluster; five cells hold 2-compartment full-depth bins as open shelving (bins on (0,0), (1,0), (-1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1)).
Two drawers (drawer:0#0,1#cut and drawer:0#1,1#cut) sit on the cut faces of the half-n bases at (0,1) and (1,1).

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it has no load rating or strength model, so no 50 kg rating can be verified. Nothing in the build establishes that capacity; the printed material and joints would need testing by the user.

requirements.requirement: House rules: close open faces with caps
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces was refused with MESH_CLASH (cap would run into the drawer frame), so 16 open faces remain uncapped. lockJoints applied (10 joint bolts) and check_build reports meshClash clear with no errors.
Book props would not rest in the 2-compartment bins (PROP_NO_REST, overlaps cell wall), so no books are shown in the build.

finish.summary: Built a hex-base shelf unit: 7 bases on the ground level, 5 open shelf cells with 2-compartment bins, and 2 drawers on half-base cut faces. Joints are locked and the mesh check is clear. Two gaps: the 50 kg book rating cannot be verified by the configurator (it checks fit only, so that requirement is unmet), and capping the open faces was refused because a cap clashes with a drawer frame, so the unit is not fully closed. Books do not fit the bins as props, so the unit is shown empty.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
